messages:
Elena (CEO): Thanks everyone for coming to the all-hands Q&A today — quick live thread for the ops/process questions about releases, oncall, quality bars and SLAs. I'll kick off with the top ask: what is our expected release cadence for infra/runtime changes going forward?
Matt (VP Eng): Short answer: aim for a biweekly stable release window for infra/runtime, with hotfix lanes for critical patches. Longer term we want monthly major drops.
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): To add: biweekly cadence applies when change has perf/regression sign-off. We'll keep a weekly triage cut to decide if it ships in the next window.
Sam (Staff SWE): Clarifying — is the triage cut a hard blocker? e.g., code merged after cut waits for next window?
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): Yes — merges after cut default to next window unless labeled emergency. Use label `release:hotfix` + @matt for exceptions.
Maya (SRE): For oncall impact, please include rollout plan + blast radius notes in PRs. If you touch KV cache or routing, flag the oncall channel early.
Oliver (PM): Will product changes follow same cadence or have separate faster lanes?
Matt (VP Eng): Product-facing feature ships can be toggled behind flags and follow a feature rollout plan. Non-flagged product changes should align to the same windows for predictability.
Sam (Staff SWE): About quality bars — are we updating the bar to require perf/statistical smoke tests for any runtime change?
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): We'll require a perf check for changes touching runtime kernels, batching, kv cache or scheduler. Tests: regression benchmark + unit smoke that runs in CI. If perf delta > 5% p50 latency, you need a mitigation plan.
Maya (SRE): Also adding SLA considerations: customer-facing routes with SLA tags (S1/S2) must have fallback policies configured and can use dedicated capacity. Ops will prevent risky rollouts to S1 without an explicit canary and rollback plan.
Elena (CEO): Can the eng teams get a one-pager on the new cut dates, labels, and SLA mapping? That would help PMs and Eng managers.
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): I'll publish the one-pager to the handbook by EOD Friday. It will include: triage cut times, label policy, perf thresholds, rollback steps, and who to ping.
Sam (Staff SWE): Nice — can we also get a small snippet for PR templates to ensure rollout notes and blast radius are included?
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): Yep — will include PR template examples in the doc.
Oliver (PM): For roadmap transparency — will releases be visible in the console or calendar?
Matt (VP Eng): We'll add a public calendar feed and a per-release changelog in the Console -> Operations tab. ETA: next quarter.
Elena (CEO): Good. Quick question on SLAs: how do we measure customer-impacting incidents vs tolerable latency spikes?
Maya (SRE): We use token-level latency distribution per route + error budget. If error budget burn crosses 30% in a rolling 7-day window we trigger remediation actions (rate-limits, routing to dedicated capacity, rollback). I'll share the incident playbook link.
deploy-bot: Reminder: weekly release triage happens every Tue 11:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).
Sam (Staff SWE): Action items for me: update runtime PR template, add perf smoke for kernel changes.
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): Action items for me: publish one-pager + PR snippets, update triage calendar invite with cut time.
Maya (SRE): I'll add SLA thresholds and incident hooks to the playbook.
Elena (CEO): Thanks all. If there's anything unresolved, drop follow-ups here or ping me directly. :raised_hands:
Sam (Staff SWE): One follow-up — can we make the `release:hotfix` process explicit in the handbook with example commands for emergency hotfix deploys?
Jordan (Dir Eng Ops): Will do. Also adding a short checklist for oncall handoffs during a release window.
Oliver (PM): Thanks — this cleared a lot. I'll sync w/ product leads and reopen if needed. :thumbsup:
